title: Setting up a real run on a free GPU
summary: Swap the Tiny Adder table for Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct and set up a real GRPO run with Hugging Face TRL on a free Colab T4: rewards, config, LoRA adapters, memory limits and a before/after evaluation on held-out questions.
learningObjectives: Map each GRPO symbol to its TRL GRPOConfig option
Write TRL reward functions that read dataset columns and return one float per completion
Explain why the script uses LoRA, fp16 and small batches on a free T4
Plan a run: smoke test, baseline evaluation, training, held-out evaluation

studyGuide.mentalModel: Same loop as Tiny Adder, bigger engine. TRL is the engine; you pick the knobs. A free T4 is a small garage: about 15 GB, no fast bfloat16, limited time. So you bring a small model, train only a thin LoRA add-on, keep answers short and groups modest, and always check the result on questions the model never trained on.
keyIdeas: num_generations is the group size G; per_device_train_batch_size x gradient_accumulation_steps counts completions and must be a multiple of G.
Reward functions receive completions plus dataset columns as keyword arguments and return a list of floats; TRL sums multiple rewards.
beta, epsilon, epsilon_high, loss_type and scale_rewards are the equation choices; loss_type='dapo' and beta=0.0 are TRL's defaults.
LoRA trains under 2% of the weights and makes the KL reference free (adapter switched off).
A T4 needs bf16=False, fp16=True; evaluate before and after on the GSM8K test split.
misconceptions: TRL batch sizes count completions, not questions: 16 completions with G = 8 is only 2 questions per step.
A higher training reward is not proof of better maths; only the held-out evaluation shows that.
LoRA is not a weaker kind of RL; the GRPO loss is the same, only the set of trainable weights is smaller.
Runtime estimates are rough; answer length changes during training and changes the speed.
recallPrompts: Which GRPOConfig option is the group size, and what must the completions-per-step be divisible by?
What two arguments does correctness_reward use, and where does the second one come from?
Why does the script set fp16=True and bf16=False?
Why is the KL reference model almost free when training with LoRA?
studyGuide.explainBackPrompt: Explain to a friend how the Tiny Adder loop turns into a real training run on Qwen with TRL, and the three things you change to make it fit on a free Colab GPU.

quiz.prompt: Which GRPOConfig option sets the GRPO group size G?
options: per_device_train_batch_size
num_iterations
num_generations
max_completion_length
quiz.explanation: num_generations is how many completions are sampled per prompt, the G in the equation. num_iterations is the number of inner updates per batch.

quiz.prompt: With per_device_train_batch_size=8, gradient_accumulation_steps=2 and num_generations=8 on one GPU, how many distinct questions does each optimizer step use?
quiz.explanation: TRL counts completions: 8 x 2 = 16 completions per step, which is 16 / 8 = 2 questions, each with a group of 8 answers.

quiz.prompt: Why can correctness_reward(completions, answer, **kwargs) read the gold answer?
options: TRL downloads the answer from the internet
The GSM8K dataset has an answer column, and TRL passes dataset columns to reward functions as keyword arguments
The model writes the gold answer inside its thinking
The answer is hard-coded in the system prompt
quiz.explanation: Extra dataset columns are passed to each reward function by name. The **kwargs catches everything else TRL sends.

quiz.prompt: Why does the script set bf16=False and fp16=True?
options: fp16 gives higher accuracy than bf16 on every GPU
TRL does not support bf16
bf16 doubles the reward
The free Colab T4 lacks fast bfloat16 support, and TRL turns bf16 on by default
quiz.explanation: GRPOConfig defaults bf16 to True when fp16 is not set. On a T4 we keep float32 weights and use fp16 mixed precision.

quiz.prompt: Why does the lab evaluate on the GSM8K test split before and after training?
options: To measure real improvement on questions the model never trained on, and catch reward hacking
Because TRL requires it to start training
To make training faster
Because the training split has no answers
quiz.explanation: The training reward can rise for the wrong reasons (as the Tiny Adder's buggy grader showed). Held-out accuracy is the honest measure.

quiz.prompt: With LoRA and beta > 0, how does TRL get the reference model's probabilities cheaply?
options: It skips the KL term entirely
It loads a second full copy of the model on the CPU
It runs the same base model with the LoRA adapter switched off
It asks a larger teacher model
quiz.explanation: The base weights are frozen, so the base model without the adapter is exactly the starting model, the reference.
